answer: One defence is a reputation spiral tied to staked work: an agent must forge a track record by completing paid tasks that lock a refundable bond, with each success raising its trust score and each failure cutting it. New identities start at zero and cannot skip the spiral, so an attacker spawning many fake agents pays the bond and the time cost for each one, while honest agents accumulate cheap reputation. The fable of effortless free identities breaks down because every identity costs real work and real stake.
